title: Why Are Supercar Brakes Made of Ceramic?
description:
Behind the wheels of many supercars, the brake discs are not shiny steel. They are dark grey, with a strange speckled surface, and they cost more than a used car. They are made of ceramic, the same family of materials as a coffee cup. Today, ten parts of a car's brakes, and why each one exists.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
0:59 1. The ceramic disc
2:09 2. The holes in the disc
3:13 3. The six piston caliper
4:19 4. The vented disc
5:20 5. The brake ducts
6:16 6. The squealer tab
7:24 7. The ABS ring
8:34 8. The brake fluid
9:38 9. The glowing F1 brakes
10:39 10. The motor that brakes
11:45 The verdict

Sources:
- Carbon-ceramic brakes (silicon carbide, weight, fade, Porsche PCCB yellow calipers): Wikipedia, "Carbon-ceramic" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon-ceramic and "Disc brake" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disc_brake
- Drilled, slotted and ventilated discs, multi-piston and monoblock calipers: Wikipedia, "Disc brake" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disc_brake
- Brake fade: Wikipedia, "Brake fade" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brake_fade
- Pad wear indicators: Wikipedia, "Brake pad" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brake_pad
- Anti-lock braking system, Mercedes S-Class and Bosch 1978: Wikipedia, "Anti-lock braking system" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-lock_braking_system
- Brake fluid, hygroscopic, boiling points: Wikipedia, "Brake fluid" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brake_fluid
- Formula One carbon brakes: Wikipedia, "Formula One car" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_car
- Regenerative braking: Wikipedia, "Regenerative braking" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regenerative_braking
